title: Ethanol and HBr
subtitle: Protonation turns OH into a leaving group

reactants.caption: ethanol + HBr
reactants.learnerPrompt: Hydroxide cannot leave. Show how the acid helps.
hintTiers: Hydroxide is a poor leaving group. How can the OH group be made into a better one?
The oxygen of ethanol takes the proton of HBr; the H–Br pair goes onto bromine. Two arrows.
Arrow 1: a lone pair on the oxygen forms a bond to the hydrogen of HBr. Arrow 2: the H–Br bond breaks, and its pair goes onto bromine.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Hydroxide is a strong base and a very poor leaving group. Protonate the oxygen first, so that water leaves instead.
Bromide cannot push out hydroxide, a very poor leaving group. The acid must protonate the oxygen first.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the oxygen takes the proton. Hydrogen can only have one bond, so what happens to the H–Br bond?

oxonium-ion.caption: ethyloxonium ion + bromide
oxonium-ion.learnerPrompt: Bromide now displaces water. Draw the arrows.
hintTiers: The carbon is primary, so a carbocation will not form. Which mechanism is left?
Bromide attacks the CH₂ carbon from the back as the C–O bond breaks and water leaves. Two arrows.
Arrow 1: a lone pair on bromide forms a bond to the CH₂ carbon. Arrow 2: the C–O bond breaks, and its pair goes onto the oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That just gives back ethanol and HBr. Use bromide as a nucleophile at carbon instead.
The CH₃ carbon has no leaving group. Attack the CH₂ carbon, bonded to the oxygen.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Water would leave, but a primary carbocation is far too unstable to form. On a primary carbon, bromide pushes in as water leaves: SN2.
Octet check: carbon would now have 10 electrons. What has to leave as the nucleophile arrives?

steps.explanationAfterStep: The OH group is now OH₂⁺: it can leave as a neutral water molecule, a good leaving group.
Water is a good leaving group because it is neutral and stable. On a primary carbon the substitution is SN2.

mechanismSummary: Converting an alcohol to an alkyl bromide: acid makes the leaving group (OH becomes OH₂⁺), then bromide displaces water. A primary alcohol reacts by SN2; a tertiary one would react by SN1.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 15
